builds.name: Reference: Contact fighter
builds.goal: Reference for Gnar: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A form-timed fighter who kites through Mini Gnar's three-hit pattern before converting rage into Mega Gnar disruption. Build value changes with the form and timing of the fight. Fix Mini versus Mega form and rage timing. An attack route must repay lost Mega durability; test Mini three-hit damage and Mega engage separately. Stridebreaker access and conditional Sundered Sky sustain may buy time for repeated kit damage.
testPlan: Kit question for Gnar: Fix Mini versus Mega form and rage timing. An attack route must repay lost Mega durability; test Mini three-hit damage and Mega engage separately.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then Sundered Sky) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Rage. Do not treat mana regeneration as Rage recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Stridebreaker access and conditional Sundered Sky sustain may buy time for repeated kit damage. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Gnar throws a boomerang that damages and slows enemies it hits before returning to him. If he catches the boomerang its cooldown is reduced.

Mega Gnar instead throws a boulder that stops on the first unit hit, damaging and slowing everything nearby. It can then be picked up to reduce the cooldown. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Physical pressure or sustained contact must justify these purchases; MR and healing slots are matchup dependent.

Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Physical pressure or sustained contact must justify these purchases; MR and healing slots are matchup dependent.
Full cost 16,800 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then Sundered Sky. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Sterak's Gage, Death's Dance, Spirit Visage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Rage. Do not treat mana regeneration as Rage recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

kitEvidence.formula: Mini Gnar Passive: Every third Attack or Ability on the same enemy deals an additional @spell.GnarW:MiniTotalDamage@ plus @spell.GnarW:MiniPercentHPDamage*100@% max Health magic damage and grants @spell.GnarR:RHyperMovementSpeedPercent@% Move Speed decaying over @spell.GnarW:MiniHasteDuration@ seconds.

Mini Gnar Passive: Increase Hyper's Move Speed.

Mega Gnar: Gnar tosses nearby enemies, dealing [200 / 300 / 400 + (1) × AP + (0.5) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage, Knocking Back, and Slowing them by [45]% for [1.25 / 1.5 / 1.75] seconds. Enemies that hit a wall instead take [(200 / 300 / 400 + (1) × AP + (0.5) × AD[statFormula=2]) × ((150) × (0.01))] physical damage and are Stunned.

Mini Gnar: Gnar throws a boomerang that deals @spell.GnarQ:MiniTotalDamage@ physical damage and Slows by @spell.GnarQ:SlowAmount*100@% for @spell.GnarQ:SlowDuration@ seconds. The boomerang returns after hitting an enemy, dealing reduced damage to subsequent targets. Each enemy can only be hit once. Catching the boomerang reduces its Cooldown by @spell.GnarQ:MiniCDRefund*100@%.

Gnar generates Rage by dealing and receiving damage. At max Rage his next Ability transforms him into Mega Gnar for 15 seconds.

Mini Gnar: Gain [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=0, perLevel=1, changes=[{"mLevel": 16, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 2.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}])] Move Speed, [characterLevelInterpolation(0.055 → 0.99; raw flags preserved)] Attack Speed, and [characterLevelInterpolation(0 → 100; raw flags preserved)] Attack Range.

Mega Gnar: Gain [UNRESOLVED({ee18a47b}; see calculationRaw)] max Health, [characterLevelInterpolation(3.5 → 54.5; raw flags preserved)] Armor, [characterLevelInterpolation(3.5 → 63; raw flags preserved)] Magic Resist, and [characterLevelInterpolation(6 → 48.5; raw flags preserved)] Attack Damage.

Mini Gnar: Gnar leaps, gaining @spell.GnarE:MinibAS*100@% Attack Speed for @spell.GnarE:MiniASDuration@ seconds. If Gnar lands on a unit he will bounce off it, traveling further. Bouncing off an enemy deals @spell.GnarE:MiniTotalDamage@ physical damage and briefly Slows by @spell.GnarE:MoveSpeedMod*-100@%.
